meta.description: Enables cardholders to pay their credit card account balance in full through an online bill payment transaction.
meta.process_description: The program presents a bill payment screen where a customer service representative or cardholder enters an account ID to retrieve the current outstanding balance. The user must explicitly confirm the payment (Y/N) before the transaction is processed. Upon confirmation, the program creates a full-balance payment transaction record in the transaction file, then updates the account balance to zero by subtracting the paid amount. The payment is recorded as a 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE' transaction with type code '02', category code '2', and a system-generated unique transaction ID with timestamps.

files.ACCTDAT: Credit card account master file storing current balance and account details
files.TRANSACT: Transaction history file where the bill payment transaction record is written
files.CXACAIX: Cross-reference index file linking account IDs to card numbers, used to retrieve the card number associated with the account being paid

business_rules: Account ID must not be empty; the payment cannot proceed without a valid account identifier.
The customer must explicitly confirm the payment by entering 'Y' before any funds are applied; entering 'N' cancels and clears the screen.
Only valid confirmation values are accepted (Y/y or N/n); any other value triggers an error message.
A bill payment can only be processed if the account has a positive outstanding balance; accounts with zero or negative balance are rejected with the message 'You have nothing to pay'.
The payment always covers the full current account balance — partial payments are not supported by this program.
After a confirmed payment, the account balance is reduced to zero by computing: new balance = current balance minus payment amount.
Each bill payment generates a new unique transaction ID by reading the last transaction ID and incrementing it by 1.
The payment transaction is timestamped with both origination and processing timestamps set to the same current system time.
Navigation: PF3 returns the user to the previous screen (defaulting to the main menu COMEN01C), and PF4 clears the current screen.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group containing all operational variables used during the online bill payment process, including program identity, file references, flags, and transaction data.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this bill payment program ('COBIL00C'), used for identification in screen headers, error logging, and inter-program communication to indicate which program is currently executing.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier ('CB00') assigned to the online bill payment screen, used by the system to route user requests to this specific program and to track which transaction is active in the session.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: A general-purpose message area used to display informational or error messages to the cardholder on the bill payment screen, such as validation errors, confirmation prompts, or success notifications.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the transaction history file ('TRANSACT') where each completed bill payment is recorded as a new transaction entry, creating a permanent audit trail of the payment.

variables.name: WS-ACCTDAT-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the credit card account master file ('ACCTDAT') that holds the cardholder's current balance and account details, which is read to retrieve the balance due and updated to zero after a successful payment.

variables.name: WS-CXACAIX-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the cross-reference index file ('CXACAIX') that links an account ID to its associated card number, used during bill payment to retrieve the card number needed to write the transaction record.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator flag that controls whether the bill payment process should be halted and a validation message displayed to the user. When set to 'Y', processing stops and the error is shown on screen; 'N' means no errors have been detected and processing can continue.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name indicating that a validation error has been detected during bill payment processing (e.g., missing account ID, invalid confirmation value, or zero balance), causing the program to stop and display an error message to the cardholder.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no validation errors have been detected and the bill payment process may proceed normally through its next steps.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each file I/O or system service call (such as reading the account record or writing the transaction), used to detect whether the operation succeeded or encountered a system-level error during payment processing.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code that provides additional detail about why a file or system operation failed, used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose and handle specific error conditions during the bill payment transaction.

variables.name: WS-USR-MODIFIED
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the cardholder has modified any input field on the bill payment screen during the current interaction, used to determine whether the screen data needs to be re-validated before processing the payment.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the cardholder has changed one or more input fields on the bill payment screen, triggering re-validation of the entered data before the payment is processed.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the cardholder has not changed any input fields on the bill payment screen since the last display, meaning previously validated data can be reused without re-validation.

variables.name: WS-CONF-PAY-FLG
variables.description: The payment confirmation flag capturing the cardholder's explicit intent to pay their full outstanding balance. A value of 'Y' authorizes the system to apply the payment and zero out the account balance; 'N' cancels the payment and clears the screen. Any other value is rejected as invalid.

variables.name: CONF-PAY-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating the cardholder has explicitly confirmed they wish to pay their full outstanding credit card balance, authorizing the system to proceed with applying the payment and writing the transaction record.

variables.name: CONF-PAY-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating the cardholder has declined to proceed with the bill payment, causing the program to cancel the transaction and clear the payment screen without making any changes to the account balance.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT
variables.description: The dollar amount of the bill payment transaction, always equal to the full current outstanding balance on the account. This amount is applied to reduce the account balance to zero and is recorded in the transaction history file as the payment amount.

variables.name: WS-CURR-BAL
variables.description: The current outstanding balance on the cardholder's credit card account before the payment is applied, read from the account master file. This value is displayed to the cardholder and used to determine the payment amount. If zero or negative, the payment is rejected with a 'nothing to pay' message.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-ID-NUM
variables.description: The system-generated unique identifier assigned to this bill payment transaction, created by reading the last transaction ID in the file and incrementing it by 1. This ID uniquely identifies the payment in the transaction history for audit and reconciliation purposes.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-DATE
variables.description: The date on which the bill payment transaction is processed, formatted as MM/DD/YY, captured from the current system date at the time of payment. This date is recorded in the transaction history to document when the payment was made.

variables.name: WS-ABS-TIME
variables.description: The absolute system timestamp retrieved at the time of payment processing, used to derive the current date and time that are stamped on the bill payment transaction record as both the origination and processing timestamps.

variables.name: WS-CUR-DATE-X10
variables.description: The current calendar date formatted as a 10-character string (e.g., MM/DD/YYYY), derived from the system timestamp, used to populate the transaction date fields in the bill payment record and display the current date on the payment screen.

variables.name: WS-CUR-TIME-X08
variables.description: The current time of day formatted as an 8-character string (e.g., HH:MM:SS), derived from the system timestamp, used to populate the transaction time fields in the bill payment record and display the current time on the payment screen.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-INFO
variables.description: A group of fields used to maintain session state for the CB00 bill payment transaction across screen interactions, including transaction ID range boundaries, pagination state, and the currently selected transaction — supporting navigation and context retention between user interactions.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-TRNID-FIRST
variables.description: The transaction ID of the first transaction in the current page or range being displayed to the user, used to maintain the user's position within the transaction list during navigation of the bill payment history.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-TRNID-LAST
variables.description: The transaction ID of the last transaction in the current page or range being displayed, used as a boundary marker to determine where the next page of transaction history begins during user navigation.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The current page number within the transaction history listing, used to track and display the cardholder's position as they navigate through multiple pages of bill payment or transaction records.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether additional pages of transaction records exist beyond the current page being displayed, used to control forward navigation availability in the transaction history listing.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that more transaction records exist beyond the current page, enabling the user to navigate forward to view additional bill payment history entries.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the current page is the last page of transaction records, meaning there are no further entries to display and forward navigation should be disabled.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-TRN-SEL-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the cardholder has selected a specific transaction from the list for further action or detail viewing, used to control subsequent processing based on the user's selection.

variables.name: CDEMO-CB00-TRN-SELECTED
variables.description: The transaction ID of the specific transaction record selected by the cardholder from the transaction list, carried forward to the next program or screen to retrieve and display the full details of that particular bill payment or transaction.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area used to pass data between program invocations and between this bill payment program and other programs in the CardDemo application, preserving session context such as account information, user identity, and navigation state across screen transitions.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: The linkage area placeholder within the CICS communication area, representing the data passed into this bill payment program from the calling program (such as account ID and user context), enabling the program to know which account to process the payment for and who initiated the request.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration paragraph that controls the entire bill payment session flow. It determines whether to initialize a new session, process user input, or handle navigation actions, then returns control to the CICS transaction manager to await the next user interaction.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full bill payment workflow when the user submits the payment screen: it validates the account ID and confirmation input, retrieves the current balance, and — upon explicit customer confirmation — creates a payment transaction record and zeroes out the account balance.

paragraphs.name: GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP
paragraphs.description: Captures the exact current system date and time to serve as the official timestamp for the bill payment transaction. This timestamp is recorded on the payment record to document precisely when the transaction was originated and processed.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Handles the user's request to exit the bill payment screen and return to the previous application screen. It ensures a safe handoff back to the calling screen (defaulting to the sign-on screen if no prior navigation context exists), passing along the identity of the current program before transferring control.

paragraphs.name: SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Prepares and displays the bill payment screen to the user, including any status or error messages, so the cardholder or representative can view the current payment details and take action. This is the final step in rendering the payment interface after all data has been assembled.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-BILLPAY-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Captures the data entered by the user on the bill payment screen, collecting the account ID and payment confirmation choice submitted by the customer service representative or cardholder. This is the entry point for processing any user input before validation and payment execution begin.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the standard screen header area with current date, time, application titles, transaction name, and program identity before displaying the bill payment screen to the user. This ensures every screen presented to the customer service representative carries consistent, accurate contextual information for audit and navigation purposes.

paragraphs.name: READ-ACCTDAT-FILE
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the credit card account record from the account master file using the provided account ID, locking it for update to ensure data integrity during payment processing. Handles cases where the account is not found or a system error occurs by halting the payment and notifying the user.

paragraphs.name: UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE
paragraphs.description: Persists the updated account record — with the balance reduced to zero — back to the account master file after a confirmed bill payment. Handles any file update failures by alerting the user and halting further payment processing.

paragraphs.name: READ-CXACAIX-FILE
paragraphs.description: Looks up the card number associated with the account being paid by searching the cross-reference index using the entered account ID. Handles cases where the account is not found or the lookup fails, preventing the payment from proceeding without a valid linked card.

paragraphs.name: STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initiates a browse (sequential read) of the transaction history file, starting from a specific transaction ID position, in order to locate the most recently recorded transaction. This is a prerequisite step to determining the last-used transaction ID so that a new unique ID can be generated for the incoming bill payment.

paragraphs.name: READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the most recent transaction record from the transaction history file in reverse order, in order to determine the last used transaction ID so that a new unique ID can be generated for the incoming bill payment. It handles both successful retrieval and edge cases such as an empty file or system errors.

paragraphs.name: ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: Closes the sequential browse operation on the transaction history file after the last transaction ID has been read and incremented. This step is required to release the file cursor before a new payment transaction record can be written.

paragraphs.name: WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph physically records the confirmed bill payment transaction into the transaction history file, then informs the user of the outcome — displaying a success confirmation with the unique transaction reference, or an appropriate error message if the write operation fails.

paragraphs.name: CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Resets the bill payment screen to a clean state by clearing all entered data and redisplaying a blank payment form. This allows a customer service representative or cardholder to start a new payment entry without residual data from a previous session.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: Resets the bill payment screen to a clean, empty state by clearing all user-facing input fields and any informational messages. This ensures no residual data from a previous transaction is visible or carried forward when the screen is refreshed or reused.
